messages:
alex: Seeing flaky 403s from the API during our CI deploys, only since the token refresh change earlier today.

alex: Example: job runs, runner sidecar calls token-refresh, then the deploy step hits Redwood API with 403 on the first request after refresh. Subsequent retry succeeds.

alex: Error snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{"error":"Forbidden","message":"imposter: token window expired or insufficient scope"}
x-request-id: rwd-8a9f2
```

maya: thanks — can you paste the runner sidecar logs around the refresh time and the token TTL the provider returned?

alex: paste: `refresh_response: {"access_token":"***","expires_in":25}`

alex: sidecar log: `cached_token_age=0.5s cache_ttl=50s using_cached=false` then later `deploy_request start -> 403`

jon: interesting — provider handed a 25s TTL but our cache kept the token for up to 50s. jitter on refresh + clock skew could make the token effectively negative when used.

samir: is this the new short-lived-token policy from infra? I pushed a change to reduce max TTL to 30s for those service accounts.

alex: yes that change landed ~09:10 UTC. We see failures in ~09:12-09:18 window.

maya: repro idea: run a loop locally that requests a token with expires_in=25, then sleep 0.5s and immediately call the API. repeat to get a fail rate. also check runner-config `token_cache_window` value.

alex: repro script I used: `for i in {1..100}; do curl -s "$TOKEN_ENDPOINT" | jq -r .expires_in; sleep 0.5; curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $REDWOOD_API/v1/deploy || echo "fail"; done` -> ~12% fails

jon: if cache TTL > provider TTL we need to enforce cache_max_age = min(provider.expires_in, configured_window) and subtract safety margin. right now we don't.

infra-bot: deploy-bot reported 403 for job ci/deploy/42 (rwd-8a9f2). Auto-incident-log appended.

maya: temporary mitigation: bump token_cache_window to 20s and set a safety subtract (token_safety_margin=5s) in runner config. long-term: treat provider.expires_in as authoritative and jitter-refresh earlier.

samir: I'll revert the infra TTL change to 60s for the affected service account while we fix the runner code.

alex: thanks — can you also whitelist retries so the first 403 triggers an immediate refresh+retry instead of failing job? right now it marks the job failed after single attempt.

maya: yes we can flip that flag in the runner feature gate (ci.retry_on_auth_failure=true). I'll schedule a patch to the runner image.

jon: assigned to me to add robust cache logic: enforce cache_max_age = min(provider_ttl - safety_margin, configured_window) and add clock_skew compensation of 2s. Will open PR and link.

alex: appreciate it — tagging me on the PR, I can validate with our project. :thumbsup:

maya: follow-ups: (1) samir to revert TTL change, (2) jon to send PR, (3) maya to flip retry_on_auth_failure in canary runners.

samir: reverting now and pinging once done.

deploy-bot: deployment job ci/deploy/42 retried automatically after token refresh and completed successfully.

alex: confirmed one successful run now. will monitor for next hour and report if anything else crops up.
